simple.meaning: מָשַׁךְ (mâshak) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to draw , used in a great variety of applications (including to sow , to sound , to prolong , to develop , to march , to remove , to delay , to be tall , etc.).” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 36 times across Genesis, Exodus, Deuteronomy, Joshua, Judges, and 13 more, beginning at Genesis 37:28. Its contexts include family line, city, mountain, Egypt, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מָשַׁךְ (H4900).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: מָשַׁךְ (mâshak) / H4900 is traced through Genesis 37:28, Exodus 12:21, Exodus 19:13, Deuteronomy 21:3 as a generated source-based concept entry.
